scope: Open review of status asthmaticus management in the paediatric ICU.

keyRecommendations.text: Status asthmaticus is described with inhaled beta-agonists, oral or IV steroids, and oxygen, and usually needs hospital admission.
Nebulized ipratropium in the PICU is given at 125–500 mcg/dose every 4–6 hours.
About 5% of PICU admissions with status asthmaticus in a 2009–2019 database required intubation, and that percentage decreased over time.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat status asthmaticus with beta-agonists, systemic steroids, and oxygen; add ipratropium in the stated PICU dose range; intubation is uncommon and became less frequent in the cited database.
notableCaveats: The source is a paediatric ICU review. Adult BTS dose tables are not in this text.

source.title: Status Asthmaticus in the Pediatric ICU: A Comprehensive Review of Management and Challenges.
